case.caveats: Five-primer multiplex cocktail (AMOS-PCR): one IS711 primer at 1 uM plus four species-specific primers at 0.2 uM each, so the intended reaction is multi-primer, not a simple pair. The IS711 primer matches 17 sites on CP000708.1 (multi-locus by design); only one pairs productively with the B. ovis primer, which lies in the bcsp31/BCSP31K gene upstream of the B. ovis IS711 copy. Correct orientation is IS711 primer forward / B. ovis primer reverse. A second in-silico pair of 13,980 bp also exists on this template and would not amplify under the paper's 2-min extension. Independently verified: exact 976-bp product at 1175240..1176215 on CP000708.1, against a size the paper read from a 1.5% agarose gel versus a 100-bp ladder.
case.citation: Bricker BJ, Halling SM. Differentiation of Brucella abortus bv. 1, 2, and 4, Brucella melitensis, Brucella ovis, and Brucella suis bv. 1 by PCR. J Clin Microbiol. 1994;32(11):2660-2666. doi:10.1128/jcm.32.11.2660-2666.1994. PMID 7852552.
case.element: IS711 (IS711/IS6501 insertion sequence) - species-specific IS711 insertion-site PCR
case.loci_justification: AMOS-PCR is run at the bench as a five-primer multiplex; the pair scored here is the species-specific pair for this template, and the IS711 copy it reports is a single chromosomal locus. Filed under the 'irap-remap' panel for convenience, which is a label and not a statement about locus multiplicity.

case.where_in_paper: Table 2 ('Sequences of oligonucleotide primers for PCR') gives the IS711-specific and B. ovis-specific primers verbatim; Results section 'Amplification of DNA fragments from the 19 Brucella biovars by PCR with a primer cocktail' and Fig. 2 give the 976-bp size.
case.worked_prediction_note: The entry records a worked prediction — a coordinate range, an in-silico check, or a sequence-derived length — so the expected answer was written down before the engine ran. The published size remains external, but this case was not scored blind.
